summary: Yorba Linda is the birthplace of Richard Nixon — and the presidential library and museum still sits on the original nine-acre citrus farm where he grew up, making it one of the few presidential birthplaces you can visit in the middle of a Southern California suburb. That quirky historical footnote aside, the city's defining physical feature is its eastern edge, where planned subdivisions climb into the rolling hills of the Chino Hills and Santiago Canyon, giving higher-elevation homes genuine sunset views over Orange County's coastal plain. The terrain feeds directly into outdoor access: trails in Chino Hills State Park and the adjacent Santiago Oaks Regional Park put serious canyon hiking within minutes of residential streets. Financially, the home-value-to-income ratio sits around 7.2×, steep even by Orange County standards, and monthly rent at $2,779 consumes roughly 22% of the median household's gross income — comfortable on paper, but the purchase math is far harder. The violent crime rate of 46.6 per 100,000 is remarkably low, while larceny at 823 per 100,000 accounts for the vast majority of reported offenses. With 76°F average daytime highs and 9.4 hours of daily sunshine, the climate barely fluctuates season to season. Yorba Linda functions largely as a bedroom community — no single major employer anchors the city itself, and the 91 and 57 freeways funnel commuters toward Anaheim, Irvine, and beyond. It's a place where the geography is genuinely striking but the daily rhythm revolves almost entirely around the car.
